svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.15.2.3 Pier-Type Foundations
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.15 FOOTINGS AND FOUNDATIONS
Pier-Type Foundations

g.text: Building 4.3 m (14′-1¼″) wide or less: block
length at right angles to the building length
Height not more than 3 times the least
Piers support the principal framing members,
spaced not more than 3.5 m (11′-5¾″) apart

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where pier-type foundations are used, the
piers are designed to support the applied
loads from the superstructure
In a building of 1 storey in building height,
piers support the principal framing members
and are spaced not more than 3.5 m (11′-5¾″)
apart along the framing
Unless the piers and their footings are designed
for larger spacings.
The height of those piers does not exceed 3
times their least dimension at the base of the
pier
Concrete block piers are laid with cores
vertical
Where the building is 4.3 m (14′-1¼″) wide or
less, they are placed with their longest
dimension at right angles to the longest
dimension of the building.
Drawn: a 1-storey floor on block piers, walls above not shown. Pier footings and beam sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.15.2.3. (page 9-119)
